# awscc_eventsv2_event_source (Resource)

Resource schema for AWS::EventsV2::EventSource. A managed event source that forwards AWS service events, partner events, or events a third-party provider sends to an inbound webhook URL, onto a custom event bus.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `configuration` (Attributes) The event source configuration. Specify exactly one of AwsServiceEventsConfiguration, PartnerEventsConfiguration or WebhookEventsConfiguration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration))
- `event_bus_arn` (String) The ARN of the custom event bus the event source forwards onto.
- `name` (String) The name of the event source. The first character must be alphanumeric; the remaining characters may also include '.', '-', and '_'. Names cannot begin with the reserved aws. prefix.

### Optional

- `description` (String) A description of the event source. Control characters and Unicode line separators are not allowed.
- `details` (Attributes) Values EventBridge generated for the event source, such as a webhook's URL and the ARN of its secret. Absent for event source types that have no generated values. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--details))
- `tags` (Attributes Set) The tags assigned to the event source. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tags))

### Read-Only

- `creation_time` (String) The time the event source was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
- `event_source_arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the event source. Its resource segment has the form event-sourcev2/<type>/<name>/<id>. Amazon EventBridge sets the type segment, which is not part of the event source name. The id segment is a 25-character identifier that EventBridge generates.

Valid values for the type segment:
- aws.service - AWS service events.
- aws.partner - Partner events.
- webhook - Webhook events.
- `id` (String) Uniquely identifies the resource.
- `last_modified_time` (String) The time the event source was last modified, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.
- `revoked` (Boolean) Whether the event bus owner has revoked this event source. Revocation is permanent: a revoked event source cannot be updated, but it can be deleted.
- `state` (String) The lifecycle state of the event source: CREATING, ACTIVE, UPDATING, CREATE_FAILED, UPDATE_FAILED, DELETING, or DELETE_FAILED. Revocation by the event bus owner is reported by the Revoked property, not by the state.

<a id="nestedatt--configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration`

Optional:

- `aws_service_events_configuration` (Attributes) Configuration for forwarding a single AWS service's events. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--aws_service_events_configuration))
- `partner_events_configuration` (Attributes) Configuration for forwarding a partner event source's events. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--partner_events_configuration))
- `webhook_events_configuration` (Attributes) Configuration for receiving events that an external provider sends to a webhook URL. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--webhook_events_configuration))

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--aws_service_events_configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.aws_service_events_configuration`

Optional:

- `aws_service` (String) A single AWS service source identifier, for example aws.s3. Wildcards and lists are not allowed.
- `on_failure_configuration` (Attributes) The destination for events that could not be forwarded. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--aws_service_events_configuration--on_failure_configuration))
- `pattern` (String) A filter pattern, as a JSON string, that defines which events from the specified AWS service are forwarded to the event bus. Do not include source, account, or region as top-level fields. If you do not specify a pattern, all events from the service are forwarded.

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--aws_service_events_configuration--on_failure_configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.aws_service_events_configuration.on_failure_configuration`

Optional:

- `arn` (String) The ARN of the Amazon SQS standard queue that receives events that could not be forwarded. FIFO queues are not supported.



<a id="nestedatt--configuration--partner_events_configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.partner_events_configuration`

Optional:

- `on_failure_configuration` (Attributes) The destination for events that could not be forwarded, covering both the forwarding target and the managed partner event bus. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--partner_events_configuration--on_failure_configuration))
- `partner_bus_kms_key_identifier` (String) The identifier of the AWS KMS customer managed key for EventBridge to use, if you choose to use a customer managed key to encrypt events on the managed partner event bus. The identifier can be the key Amazon Resource Name (ARN), KeyId, key alias, or key alias ARN. If you do not specify a customer managed key identifier, EventBridge uses an AWS owned key to encrypt events on the event bus.
- `partner_event_source_arn` (String) The ARN of the partner event source to forward. The partner owns the event source, so the ARN's account segment is empty. Changing this property replaces the event source. Because Name and EventBusArn together identify an event source, and the replacement is created before the old resource is deleted, change Name in the same update.
- `pattern` (String) A filter pattern, as a JSON string, that defines which events from the specified partner event source are forwarded to the event bus. If you do not specify a pattern, all events from the partner event source are forwarded.

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--partner_events_configuration--on_failure_configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.partner_events_configuration.on_failure_configuration`

Optional:

- `arn` (String) The ARN of the Amazon SQS standard queue that receives events that could not be forwarded. FIFO queues are not supported.



<a id="nestedatt--configuration--webhook_events_configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.webhook_events_configuration`

Optional:

- `auth_configuration` (Attributes) How the provider authenticates its requests. Set exactly one authentication type. You can't change the type after you create the event source. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--webhook_events_configuration--auth_configuration))
- `deduplication_configuration` (Attributes) Deduplicates the event source's events on the event bus. If you do not specify a configuration, EventBridge does not deduplicate events. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--webhook_events_configuration--deduplication_configuration))
- `kms_key_identifier` (String) The AWS KMS key that encrypts the event source's secret in AWS Secrets Manager. If you do not specify a key, the secret is encrypted with the AWS managed key aws/secretsmanager. A key you specify must be an enabled customer managed key in your account and Region. Changing the key re-encrypts the secret under the new key. The previous key can still decrypt the stored versions until the credential is next rotated.
- `log_configuration` (Attributes) The log records Amazon EventBridge delivers for the webhook requests this event source receives. If you do not specify a configuration, EventBridge delivers no logs. Logs are delivered to the destinations you configure with Amazon CloudWatch Logs vended log delivery. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--webhook_events_configuration--log_configuration))
- `metadata_http_headers` (List of String) The HTTP request headers to add to each event's metadata, up to 20. Header names are case-insensitive and cannot repeat. Amazon EventBridge adds each header under its lowercase name. If you do not specify headers, EventBridge adds none. You cannot list headers that carry credentials or describe the network path, or the header that carries the static token.
- `role_arn` (String) The ARN of the IAM role that Amazon EventBridge assumes to put the webhook's events on the event bus. The role must belong to the calling account.

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--webhook_events_configuration--auth_configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.webhook_events_configuration.auth_configuration`

Optional:

- `basic_http_auth_configuration` (Attributes) The provider sends HTTP Basic authentication credentials. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--webhook_events_configuration--auth_configuration--basic_http_auth_configuration))
- `hmac_auth_configuration` (Attributes) The provider signs each request with a hash-based message authentication code (HMAC) of the secret. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--webhook_events_configuration--auth_configuration--hmac_auth_configuration))
- `static_token_auth_configuration` (Attributes) The provider sends the secret as the value of an HTTP header. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--webhook_events_configuration--auth_configuration--static_token_auth_configuration))

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--webhook_events_configuration--auth_configuration--basic_http_auth_configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.webhook_events_configuration.auth_configuration.basic_http_auth_configuration`

Optional:

- `password` (String) The password. Set on create only: changing this value in a template has no effect. To change the password, call RotateWebhookCredentials. The username and the webhook URL do not change.
- `username` (String) The username. Cannot contain a colon or whitespace. Changing the username requires replacing the event source, which also requires a new Name and gives the event source a new webhook URL. RotateWebhookCredentials cannot change the username.


<a id="nestedatt--configuration--webhook_events_configuration--auth_configuration--hmac_auth_configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.webhook_events_configuration.auth_configuration.hmac_auth_configuration`

Optional:

- `algorithm` (String) The hash algorithm the provider uses to compute the signature.

Valid values:
- SHA256 - SHA-256.
- SHA1 - SHA-1. Not recommended. Use SHA1 only for interoperability with a provider that cannot sign with SHA-256.
- `delimiter` (String) The separator between parts of the signature header value, for example a comma for a header value of t=1727816400,v1=<signature>, or a space when the header carries several signatures. Required when TimestampHttpHeader is the same header as SignatureHttpHeader.
- `encoding` (String) How the provider encodes the signature in the header.

Valid values:
- HEX - Hexadecimal.
- BASE64 - Base64.
- `message_id_http_header` (String) The name of the header that carries the message ID. Required when SignedMessageComposition is MESSAGE_ID_DOT_TIMESTAMP_DOT_BODY.
- `secret_encoding` (String) How the secret is encoded. RAW uses the secret's characters as the signing key. BASE64 decodes the secret first, as required by providers that issue Base64-encoded signing keys, such as those following the Standard Webhooks specification. If you do not specify an encoding, EventBridge uses RAW. Changing the encoding replaces the event source.
- `secret_value` (String) The signing key shared with the provider. If you do not specify a key, EventBridge generates one. EventBridge stores the key only in AWS Secrets Manager and never returns it. Set on create only: changing this value in a template has no effect. To change the key, call RotateWebhookCredentials. The webhook URL does not change.
- `signature_http_header` (String) The name of the header that carries the signature, for example X-Hub-Signature-256. When TimestampHttpHeader names the same header, Delimiter, SignaturePrefix and TimestampPrefix are all required.
- `signature_prefix` (String) The text that precedes the signature in the header value, for example sha256=. Required when TimestampHttpHeader is the same header as SignatureHttpHeader.
- `signed_message_composition` (String) How the provider assembles the message it signs from the request.

Valid values:
- BODY - The request body alone.
- TIMESTAMP_DOT_BODY - <timestamp>.<body>. Requires TimestampHttpHeader.
- MESSAGE_ID_DOT_TIMESTAMP_DOT_BODY - <messageId>.<timestamp>.<body>, as in the Standard Webhooks specification. Requires TimestampHttpHeader and MessageIdHttpHeader.
- `timestamp_http_header` (String) The name of the header that carries the request timestamp. Required when SignedMessageComposition is TIMESTAMP_DOT_BODY or MESSAGE_ID_DOT_TIMESTAMP_DOT_BODY, or when TimestampToleranceInSeconds is set. When it names the same header as SignatureHttpHeader, Delimiter, SignaturePrefix and TimestampPrefix are all required.
- `timestamp_prefix` (String) The text that precedes the timestamp in the header value, for example t=. Required when TimestampHttpHeader is the same header as SignatureHttpHeader.
- `timestamp_tolerance_in_seconds` (Number) The maximum difference, in seconds, allowed between the request timestamp and the time EventBridge receives the request. Requests outside this window are rejected. If you do not specify a tolerance, EventBridge uses 300 seconds. Requires TimestampHttpHeader.


<a id="nestedatt--configuration--webhook_events_configuration--auth_configuration--static_token_auth_configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.webhook_events_configuration.auth_configuration.static_token_auth_configuration`

Optional:

- `secret_value` (String) The token the provider sends in the header. If you do not specify a token, Amazon EventBridge generates one. EventBridge stores the token only in AWS Secrets Manager and never returns it. Set on create only: changing this value in a template has no effect. To change the token, call RotateWebhookCredentials. The webhook URL does not change.
- `token_http_header` (String) The name of the header that carries the secret, for example X-Webhook-Secret. Must be a valid header name as defined in RFC 7230.



<a id="nestedatt--configuration--webhook_events_configuration--deduplication_configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.webhook_events_configuration.deduplication_configuration`

Optional:

- `deduplication_type` (String) How EventBridge detects duplicate events.

Valid values:
- CONTENT_BASED - Detects duplicates by a hash of the event content.


<a id="nestedatt--configuration--webhook_events_configuration--log_configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.webhook_events_configuration.log_configuration`

Optional:

- `include_payload` (String) Whether the event payload is included in emitted log records: FULL includes it in every emitted record, and ON_ERROR_ONLY includes it only in error records. The default is ON_ERROR_ONLY.
- `level` (String) The minimum log level: OFF (no logging), ERROR, or INFO. Records below this level are not emitted. The default is OFF.




<a id="nestedatt--details"></a>
### Nested Schema for `details`

Optional:

- `webhook_details` (Attributes) Values generated for a webhook event source. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--details--webhook_details))

<a id="nestedatt--details--webhook_details"></a>
### Nested Schema for `details.webhook_details`

Read-Only:

- `secret_arn` (String) The ARN of the AWS Secrets Manager secret, in your account, that holds the webhook credential.
- `webhook_url` (String) The HTTPS URL to configure at the event provider. The URL does not change for the life of the event source. Treat the URL as a credential. The URL appears in stack describe output and in drift detection results.



<a id="nestedatt--tags"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tags`

Optional:

- `key` (String) The tag key. Unique per resource; keys are case sensitive. No leading or trailing whitespace (interior whitespace is allowed).
- `value` (String) The tag value. May be empty. No leading or trailing whitespace (interior whitespace is allowed).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = awscc_eventsv2_event_source.example
  identity = {
    event_source_arn = "event_source_arn"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `event_source_arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the event source

#### Optional

- `account_id` (String) AWS Account where this resource is managed
- `region` (String) Region where this resource is managed

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = awscc_eventsv2_event_source.example
  id = "event_source_arn"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
$ terraform import awscc_eventsv2_event_source.example "event_source_arn"
```
